newsitem.title: USA: US jobs market stable-Labor Dept economist - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: US jobs market stable-Labor Dept economist - RFTV.

text.p: The United States is enjoying a stable labor market with just enough jobs being created each month to match population growth, Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics Thomas Plewes said Friday.

"What's going on in the labor market as measured by the unemployment rate is a very stable environment," Plewes told Reuters Financial Television. "We are creating just enough jobs to take care of the growth in population and the growth in the labor force. That's a pretty good sign."
The Labor Department reported on Friday that the unemployment rate was unchanged in October at 5.2 percent.

Plewes said strikes at General Motors parts supply plants in Canada had some impact on the data, which showed employment declines in automobile manufacturing. The Canadian strike was settled, but strikes at some U.S. GM plants could have an impact on the November data if they continue into the month, Plewes said.
The October labor report showed an increase in retail employment, which Plewes said reflected optimism about the upcoming Christmas shopping season.
"Department stores added a lot more jobs than they usually do this time of month and that suggests to us perhaps there is some hope for this Christmas buying season," he said.
Labor Department economist Harvey Hamel told Reuters Financial television that the 50 cents per hour minimum wage hike on October 1 to $4.75 had no impact on the earnings data.
"There is no obvious impact of the increase in our figures," Hamel said.
